# Osprey (02, engineer) — BAD-002

## Brief
Take ads, in-app purchases and every mention of a paid plan out of the iOS app for its first App Store approval, keeping the web-side code dormant so it can come back later. The browser app at my.badtakes.io and the desktop app must not change.

Why: App Review rejected build 13003 because the binary links AppTrackingTransparency and the reviewer could not find the ATT prompt, and because Apple is asking about paid content (2.1(b)). Eric's decision is that ads and subscriptions leave the iOS build entirely, and that nothing on iOS mentions a paid plan: no Plus, lifetime, ad-free, Remove ads, subscription, upgrade or pricing copy, and no store sheet. The desktop's paid licence stays, but it unlocks nothing on iOS.

Do:
- Run `bash scripts/worktree-init.sh` first, then `npm ci` inside mobile/ (the shell is its own npm package).
- Remove `@capacitor-community/admob` and `@revenuecat/purchases-capacitor` from mobile/package.json and the lock, and re-sync so the iOS project (CapApp-SPM Package.swift and anything else cap sync writes) no longer links them.
- Remove NSUserTrackingUsageDescription, GADApplicationIdentifier and SKAdNetworkItems from mobile/ios/App/App/Info.plist, and anything else that exists only for ads, ATT or StoreKit.
- On iOS, hide every plan, tier, ad and subscription surface in web/: the plan-tier row, the Remove ads link and row, the Get Plus and ad-free buttons, the store sheet, and the paid-only account-deletion note. Key it off what the shell actually lacks (the native ads and purchases seams resolving to null, or a build-time config in the mobile build) rather than hand-listing strings, and keep mobile/ free of product logic (mobile/CLAUDE.md). A null seam must already resolve to no ad and no offer; confirm that from the code rather than assuming it.
- Make scripts/dist-ios.js and scripts/build-mobile.js stop requiring or refusing AdMob configuration if either does, so a shippable build no longer depends on it.
- Pin it with tests: extend test/build-mobile.test.js (or a sibling) so the mobile build fails if the plugins come back into mobile/package.json, if Info.plist regains the tracking keys, or if a paid-plan surface is reachable on native.
- Update docs/MOBILE-STORES.md where it states the app sells in-app purchases or shows ads (the opening facts, § A4, § A6, § B3's App Privacy table, § B8's review note, § D's ads-flag bullet), so it describes the iOS app without them and says the dormant code is re-enabled by re-adding the plugins. Leave the guest-mode and sign-in parts of the runbook alone: a later member owns them.

Verify per the repo's implementing-changes skill: `npm test`; `npm run mobile:check`, which is the unsigned simulator compile; proof that the built .app links no AppTrackingTransparency, GoogleMobileAds, UserMessagingPlatform or RevenueCat (search the built app bundle and its frameworks, and report the command you used and its output); and a simulator run signed in (the memory note mobile-ads-adfree-status describes minting a local email code against the local stack) showing no ad, plan or subscription surface, with screenshots saved under your scratchpad and their paths in your result. Do not touch the sign-in gate.
